post.caption: He carried a 138-carat ruby for luck. Rosser Reeves was an American advertising executive, and the Smithsonian says he carried this ruby as a lucky stone and called it his baby. It weighs 138.7 carats and comes from Sri Lanka. It is cut as a smooth oval, called a cabochon, and light makes a star glow across its dome. It was recut once, and that helped center the star. Reeves gave it to the Smithsonian in 1965, and the Smithsonian calls it one of the world's largest star rubies.
